children: By Jessica Flint

In 1990, Minneapolis resident Elizabeth Hyatt was browsing Unique Homes magazine when she spotted a curious listing: a 1930s French Normandy-style compound on a private island on the Canadian side of Rainy Lake, where Minnesota dissolves into Ontario wilderness.

Tired of speedboat traffic near their cabin in northern Minnesota, Elizabeth and her husband, real-estate developer Henry Hyatt, saw Rainy Lake as a sanctuary: a 360-square-mile, 2,000-island labyrinth anchored by the U.S.'s Voyageurs National Park and considerable Canadian Crown land.

When they first visited, the island was pristine but the estate was in disrepair. Built during the Great Depression as a wedding gift from an industrial heir to his wife, it was constructed by local artisans and World War I veterans who hauled materials up from shore using ponies and donkeys, according to Elizabeth. Decades later, the island couldn't power a stove and a water heater at the same time, and tap water ran bright yellow.

Elizabeth, a restorer of historic homes, initially resisted. "This is a huge project," she warned her husband, who loved the property from the start. Four years later, in 1994, they bought French Island. Elizabeth said she can't recall the purchase price.
The renovation

Elizabeth joined forces with a local contractor and spent two years modernizing infrastructure, from drilling wells to trenching power lines to re-plumbing. It took three more years before the 5,300-square-foot main lodge was livable.

Overhauling French Island has been a decadeslong project for Elizabeth, who said she is unsure of the total renovation cost. In the main lodge, original roof pitches, timber beams and seven stone fireplaces were brought back to life. An original guesthouse was revitalized.
Can't-miss features
The main lodge has 1,700 square feet of stone terraces plus a screen porch, from which views stretch over a private bay.
Original details include hand-forged iron hardware and many custom Marvin windows.
Reason for selling?

Now living on an out-of-state farm, Elizabeth, who declined to share her age, is offering the island off-market for privacy purposes. "It's about finding the right steward who wants to take care of it," she says.
What she'll miss
The absolute privacy, wildlife and magic of sitting on the front terrace overlooking the bay.
What she won't miss
"It gets to be a lot of traveling season after season," she says.
Market snapshot

French Island is an outlier on Rainy Lake for its size, privacy and amenities, says Richard Silver with Sotheby's International Realty Canada, who is the listing agent along with Neil Lyon of Sotheby's International Realty in Santa Fe, N.M. Silver says island property prices in this region vary greatly, but are often well under $1.5 million, reflecting smaller, less private and more accessible residences.
